t: Count Distinct Ways to Form Target from Two Strings
o: Each character of target is matched to an index in word1 or word2; indices used within each word must increase, and both words must contribute at least one character. This extends 'Distinct Subsequences': instead of one source string we interleave two. Counting all valid interleavings and then excluding the selections that use only one word (via ordinary Distinct Subsequences counts, with inclusion-exclusion) gives the answer. In Example 1 there are 7 unrestricted ways, minus 1 all-from-word1 minus 1 all-from-word2 = 5.
k: A 2D-prefix DP g[t][i][j] counts ways to place target[0..t) using word1[0..i) and word2[0..j), handling skips with inclusion-exclusion g[t][i-1][j] + g[t][i][j-1] - g[t][i-1][j-1].
Ways using only one word are exactly Distinct Subsequences(word, target); subtract both since target is non-empty (no double-counted 'neither' case).

a.i: g[t][i][j] = ways to form target's first t characters choosing only from word1[0..i) and word2[0..j). Recurrence: skip last index of word1 (g[t][i-1][j]), skip last of word2 (g[t][i][j-1]), add back the doubly-skipped (g[t][i-1][j-1]), plus match extensions from layer t-1 when the characters equal target[t-1]. Base g[0][i][j] = 1. Finally subtract the single-source counts.
s: Initialize layer 0 of g to all ones.
Fill layers t = 1..T using the skip/skip/match recurrence with modular arithmetic.
Compute d1 = numDistinct(word1, target) and d2 = numDistinct(word2, target) with the classic 1D DP.
a.t: O(T * n * m) time — about 1e6 states with O(1) transitions for n, m, T <= 100; O(T * n * m) space.
a.sp: O(T * n * m) — the full DP table.

a.n: Approach 2: Rolling layers to save memory
a.i: Layer t only reads layer t and layer t-1, so keeping two (n+1) x (m+1) matrices and swapping them reduces memory from O(T*n*m) to O(n*m) with identical time. Useful if constraints grow or memory limits tighten.
s: Keep previous layer gp initialized to all ones.
For each t, build the new layer gt from gp and gt itself, then swap.
Finish with the same inclusion-exclusion against the two numDistinct values.
a.t: O(T * n * m) time — same state count, constant-time transitions; O(n * m) space.
a.sp: O(n * m) — only two DP layers are retained.

w: Lead with the 3D DP; mention the rolling-layer optimization as the memory refinement. The subtle part is the 'both strings used' requirement — resolve it by inclusion-exclusion with Distinct Subsequences rather than complicating the DP state. Watch negative intermediate values after subtraction (normalize mod) and the skip-skip overlap term. Verify on Example 3, where mixed interleavings are impossible and only the two pure-block ways survive. Follow-ups: k source strings (inclusion-exclusion over 2^k subsets), or requiring the sources to alternate.
